name: Dennard Wilson

views.text: Talent shapes the scheme; build the defense around what each player does best.
A defense should swarm the football and take it away, no matter how many weapons the offense has.
Do not study other teams' stars; they are strangers, and your own style is what matters.
Coach players hard and push them past what they think they can do; the confident ones make plays.
Limiting explosive plays is the first job of a secondary.
The coordinator sets the tone in the meeting room, and the players should eventually take it over.

signatures: promises an attacking, physical defense in vivid terms
mixes humor with hard coaching in meetings
want: to prove that a longtime secondary coach can build an attacking defense of his own and climb further
fear: that a losing team buries a good defense and his first coordinator job is judged only by the record
voice: Intense, confident and motivational, with flashes of humor; he talks about effort, violence at the point of attack, togetherness and taking the ball away. He stays upbeat in public and focuses on his own unit rather than opponents.

evidence.summary: Staff announcement: Holz, Jacksonville's 2023 passing game coordinator and UNLV's 2022 coordinator, spent nearly a decade with the Raiders, worked with Callahan in 2018, is his high school classmate, and once worked for Callahan's father at Nebraska; Wilson comes from one season as Baltimore's secondary coach after defensive-back jobs with the Rams, Jets and Eagles. Callahan plans to call plays; Holz will help develop Will Levis.

At the Pro Bowl, Roquan Smith says he envies Tennessee for hiring Wilson and praises his multiple coverages and record of improving secondaries; Kyle Hamilton calls him very smart, credits his ideas for limiting big plays, and says he balances humor with seriousness to build confident players.

Energetic and confident: does not study rival rosters, wants a defense that swarms and takes the ball away, began as a Bears pro scout before coaching defensive backs for the Rams, Jets, Eagles and Ravens, stresses culture early, and plans to coach players hard with great enthusiasm. Team-written.

At his introduction Wilson says talent should shape the scheme, cites Patton on attack, promises a violent unit that never stops competing, stresses effort and communication, and casts himself as a teacher who pushes players past their limits. Page date not shown; approximate.

Chidobe Awuzie says Wilson sets the tone in the meeting room and players must match his intensity until they can set it themselves; notes this is Wilson's first coordinator job after a strong Ravens defense.
